The main restraint is a possible hurricane year and softening rates and reinsurance costs, which would pull returns down.

The 2026 nine-month run (gross loss ratio 21.0%, combined ratio 58.8%) is again close to catastrophe-free, apart from an estimated $15.0 million loss from Hurricane Isaias in Q4. Equity has since roughly doubled after the Exzeo IPO proceeds and retained earnings, so the return on the larger base will fall even if margins hold. Book growth is therefore driven by retained earnings less modest payouts, with the AOCI swing on its new bond portfolio as a further source of noise.

business_model.claim: HCI Group, Inc. primarily operates in the property and casualty insurance business, selling homeowners' property and casualty insurance products for properties in Florida and in other states in the northeast and southeast U.S., with all revenue generated in the U.S. and predominantly in Florida.
quotes: We provide various homeowners’ property and casualty insurance products for properties located in the State of Florida, which is our primary market, as well as in other states in the northeast and southeast regions of the United States (“U.S.”).
The entirety of our revenue is generated in the U.S. and predominately in the State of Florida.

business_model.claim: HCI distributes insurance policies through independent agents and expands its policy base both organically and through policy assumptions from Citizens Property Insurance Corporation and other insurers.
quotes: Our insurance business has grown both organically and through strategic policy assumptions, which have been a key driver of our expansion.

We have participated in legislatively mandated take-out programs, designed to reduce the state’s risk exposure by transitioning policies from Citizens Property Insurance Corporation (“Citizens”), a Florida state supported insurer, to private insurers.

Now and in the future, we may rely on independent agents to write our insurance policies, and if we are not able to contract with and retain independent agents, our revenues would be negatively affected.

business_model.claim: Through its publicly traded, majority-owned subsidiary Exzeo Group, Inc. (owned approximately 83.6% by HCI as of September 30, 2026), HCI provides turnkey insurance technology, operations solutions, and reinsurance placement services to property and casualty insurance carriers and agents.
quotes: Exzeo Group, Inc. (“Exzeo”), a publicly traded majority-owned subsidiary, provides turn-key insurance technology and operations solutions based on a proprietary platform of purpose-built software and data analytics applications specifically designed for the property and casualty insurance ecosystem.
In addition, Exzeo provides expert reinsurance placement services to help insurance companies manage risk by acting as an intermediary between the insurance carrier and reinsurers.
As of September 30, 2026, HCI Group, Inc. owned approximately 83.6% of Exzeo’s outstanding shares of common stock, inclusive of unvested restricted stock.

business_model.claim: HCI provides attorney-in-fact (AIF) management services for policyholder-owned reciprocal insurance exchanges (CORE and Tailrow), which HCI consolidates as primary beneficiary despite having no equity ownership in them.
quotes: We also provide attorney-in-fact (“AIF”) services for reciprocal insurance exchanges owned by their policyholders.
Although we do not have any equity interest in the reciprocal insurance exchanges, we are required to consolidate them as their primary beneficiary.

The Insurance Operations and the Reciprocal Exchange Operations record service fee expenses based on earned premiums or other appropriate measures, while Exzeo and the AIF operations recognize service fee revenue according to revenue recognition standards.

business_model.claim: HCI also operates a commercial real estate group that develops and leases commercial properties to unaffiliated tenants, as well as wholly-owned Bermuda and Cayman Islands captive reinsurance subsidiaries used to selectively retain internal risk.
quotes: Except for the undeveloped land, we generate income from our investment properties by leasing vacancies to unaffiliated tenants.
Additionally, we have a wholly-owned Bermuda domiciled captive reinsurance subsidiary which allows us to selectively retain risk and reduce the cost of third party reinsurance.
Fortex will allow us additional flexibility to selectively retain risk and reduce the cost of third-party reinsurance.

business_model.claim: HCI organizes its business into five reportable segments: Insurance Operations, Exzeo, Reciprocal Exchange Operations, Real Estate, and Corporate and Other.
quotes: We have five reportable segments: Insurance Operations, Exzeo, Reciprocal Exchange Operations, Real Estate, and Corporate and Other.

business_model.claim: Net premiums earned equal gross premiums earned less premiums ceded for catastrophe excess-of-loss, facultative, and quota-share reinsurance, where reinsurance costs vary with policy exposures, annual treaty pricing, and retrospective contract adjustments.
quotes: Our premiums ceded represent costs of reinsurance (i) to cover losses from catastrophes that exceed the retention levels defined by our catastrophe excess of loss reinsurance contracts, (ii) to provide additional loss coverage on a high-value individual risk basis through facultative reinsurance, or (iii) to assume a proportional share of losses as defined in a quota share agreement.
The rates we pay for reinsurance are based primarily on policy exposures reflected in gross premiums earned.
The decrease was a result of lower costs associated with the company’s new 2026-2027 catastrophe reinsurance programs, which began on June 1, 2026.

business_model.claim: Net investment income is earned by investing collected premiums and excess cash across available-for-sale fixed-maturity securities, equity securities, money market accounts, certificates of deposit, limited partnerships, and real estate, driven by invested asset growth and interest rates.
quotes: In the insurance industry, cash collected for premiums from policies written is invested, interest and dividends are earned thereon, and losses and loss adjustment expenses are paid out over a period of years.
Our excess cash is invested primarily in money market accounts, certificates of deposit, and available-for-sale fixed-maturity and equity securities.
